paper_title: First results of the Laser-Interferometric Detector for Axions (LIDA)
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, canonical axion-photon coupling
notes: First observing run of laser-interferometric detector for axions (LIDA). Peak sensitivity of 1.51×10^-10 GeV^-1 achieved at 1.985 neV (480.0 kHz) over 85 hours of measurement time. The detector is sensitive to polarization rotation of linearly polarized laser light induced by axion-photon coupling. Measurement band: 475.4–505.1 kHz corresponding to axion mass range 1.97–2.01 neV. Average sensitivity across the range: 3.2×10^-10 GeV^-1. No significant evidence for axions or ALPs detected. The standard local DM density of 0.3 GeV/cm^3 is assumed in the coherent field amplitude calculation (Eq. 1). This is the first detector of its kind collecting scientific data. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.85, 15)) | Vision: Figure 2 shows the sensitivity curve for LIDA's first observing run. The plot displays g_agamma (axion-photon coupling strength) vs. axion mass in meV. The x-axis spans 1.97–2.04 meV (linear scale), and the y-axis spans 1e-11 to 1e-8 GeV^-1 (log scale). The blue shaded region represents the 95% confidence level sensitivity band from the full data. The boundary traced represents the lower edge of the exclusion region (best sensitivity limit). The peak sensitivity of 1.51×10^-10 GeV^-1 is explicitly stated in the text and occurs near 1.985 meV. The curve shows a gentle downward trend across the measured mass range, indicating slightly improving sensitivity at higher masses within this narrow band.
